AI in General

How to Choose Your First AI Business Use Case

Select a small, measurable AI pilot by balancing repetition, available data, review effort and the consequences of mistakes.

By DevMania · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read

In this guide

Look for repetitive interpretation workEstimate the full effortPrefer reviewable outcomesUse a simple selection exerciseSet a stopping rule

Look for repetitive interpretation work

Start with tasks where people repeatedly read, classify or draft similar information. Examples include sorting enquiries or preparing a first draft of a project brief. Avoid beginning with a process nobody understands. If the team cannot describe a good result, it will be difficult to evaluate whether the AI output is useful.

Estimate the full effort

Count the time spent preparing input, reviewing output and correcting mistakes. A tool that drafts in seconds may still require lengthy verification. Compare the entire assisted workflow with the current process. Record a baseline from a small sample before the pilot so you have something more concrete than enthusiasm to compare against.

Prefer reviewable outcomes

A suggested category or draft response is easier to supervise than an automatic payment or account closure. For a first pilot, keep the output reversible and make the human decision visible. Choose a named owner who can judge quality and stop the trial if it creates more work than it removes.

Use a simple selection exercise

List three candidate tasks. For each, write its frequency, current effort, data availability, review method and worst plausible mistake. Select one with clear examples and manageable consequences. This is a planning exercise, not a formula that guarantees return on investment. Team capacity and operational context still matter.

Set a stopping rule

Agree what improvement would justify continuing and what errors would pause the pilot. Run it with a limited audience and compare results against the baseline. If the main problem turns out to be missing information or inconsistent processes, fix that first. An AI feature should support a useful workflow rather than conceal an unresolved one.

Published by DevMania with AI assistance. Examples illustrate planning approaches and do not claim client results. Check current provider documentation before implementing product-specific features.
